content:
"""
title: Exchange Rate Tool
author: greg
description: Real-time currency exchange rates and conversion via Frankfurter (ECB-sourced, free, no API key required)
version: 1.0
"""

import requests
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Tools:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        timeout_seconds: int = Field(
            default=10,
            description="HTTP request timeout in seconds",
        )

    def __init__(self):
        self.valves = self.Valves()
        self.citation = True

    # Common everyday names mapped to ISO 4217 codes - Frankfurter only accepts codes,
    # so this catches the phrasing people actually use ("dollars", "euros", "yen", ...)
    _ALIASES = {
        "DOLLAR": "USD",
        "DOLLARS": "USD",
        "US DOLLAR": "USD",
        "US DOLLARS": "USD",
        "EURO": "EUR",
        "EUROS": "EUR",
        "POUND": "GBP",
        "POUNDS": "GBP",
        "STERLING": "GBP",
        "BRITISH POUND": "GBP",
        "YEN": "JPY",
        "FRANC": "CHF",
        "FRANCS": "CHF",
        "SWISS FRANC": "CHF",
        "YUAN": "CNY",
        "RENMINBI": "CNY",
        "CANADIAN DOLLAR": "CAD",
        "CANADIAN DOLLARS": "CAD",
        "AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR": "AUD",
        "AUSTRALIAN DOLLARS": "AUD",
    }

    def _normalize(self, currency: str) -> str:
        cleaned = currency.strip().upper()
        return self._ALIASES.get(cleaned, cleaned)

    def get_exchange_rate(
        self, from_currency: str, to_currency: str, amount: float = 1.0
    ) -> str:
        """
        Use for any currency exchange rate or conversion question (e.g. "USD to EUR", "convert 50 GBP to JPY"). Never use web_search for these - this tool is authoritative for exchange rates.

        :param from_currency: The source currency, as an ISO code (e.g. "USD") or common name (e.g. "dollars")
        :param to_currency: The target currency, as an ISO code (e.g. "EUR") or common name (e.g. "euros")
        :param amount: The amount to convert, in from_currency. Defaults to 1 (i.e. just the raw rate).
        :return: The converted amount and the current rate, sourced from ECB daily reference rates - or an honest error message if the lookup fails.
        """
        base = self._normalize(from_currency)
        quote = self._normalize(to_currency)

        try:
            resp = requests.get(
                f"https://api.frankfurter.dev/v2/rate/{base}/{quote}",
                timeout=self.valves.timeout_seconds,
            )
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            return (
                f"Couldn't reach the exchange rate service right now ({e.__class__.__name__}). "
                f"Try again shortly, or check https://www.xe.com/currencyconverter/ directly."
            )

        if resp.status_code == 404:
            return (
                f"Couldn't find a rate for '{from_currency}' to '{to_currency}' - one or both "
                f"currency codes may not be recognized. Use standard 3-letter codes (e.g. USD, "
                f"EUR, GBP, JPY), or check https://www.xe.com/currencyconverter/ directly."
            )

        try:
            resp.raise_for_status()
            data = resp.json()
            rate = data["rate"]
            rate_date = data.get("date")
        except (requests.RequestException, KeyError, ValueError) as e:
            return (
                f"Got an unexpected response looking up {base} to {quote} "
                f"({e.__class__.__name__}). Try again shortly, or check "
                f"https://www.xe.com/currencyconverter/ directly."
            )

        converted = amount * rate
        lines = [f"{amount:,.2f} {base} = {converted:,.2f} {quote}"]
        lines.append(f"Rate: 1 {base} = {rate:.4f} {quote}")
        if rate_date:
            lines.append(
                f"As of: {rate_date} (blended daily reference rate from central bank sources, "
                f"not live intraday market data)"
            )

        return "\n".join(lines)
